description:
PR #16 review finding 3: https://github.com/jat10/zaq/pull/16
Reviewed head: 1b2637d9a5284ad7ed3febd9d175288f9dfc6897; base: f736652a1a982bf08e2ac8773f24921329d59d26.

Problem and provenance
ChannelsLive.provider_requires_global_base_url?/2 calls Bridge.capability_snapshot(provider) directly for data sources. This performs bridge selection, configuration lookup and adapter capability inspection on BO, bypassing the Channels NodeRouter boundary. In distributed deployments BO may lack the owning node's adapter configuration/dependencies; the catch-all result branch returns false, conflating unavailable capabilities with absence of a webhook/base-URL requirement.
The direct call predates PR #16. The PR retains it in the new configuration_draft/3 helper and adds another invocation on Save: handle_event("save") builds configuration_draft, then persist_modal_configuration performs the same validation again. Do not describe the entire boundary violation as newly introduced.
Evidence: lib/zaq_web/live/bo/communication/channels_live.ex configuration_draft/3 (reviewed line 1328), persist_modal_configuration/2 (around 1417), maybe_validate_global_base_url_requirement/3 and provider_requires_global_base_url?/2 (around 1613-1634). The existing test "validate requires global base URL when capability snapshot declares webhook" exercises this requirement. This finding is based on the compared execution paths; no full multi-node failure was reproduced.

Agreed direction / Action reuse assessment
Reuse load_capabilities/2, the snapshot cached on the socket, the existing :channel_capability_snapshot NodeRouter/Event request and the existing capability interpretation helper. Draft validation should derive the webhook/base-URL requirement from cached normalized facts, without invoking a bridge locally or doing per-keystroke metadata lookups. Keep authoritative save validation at the owning service boundary; inspect current ownership and route any necessary fresh capability inspection through the existing Channels event, preserving actor/opts and appropriate scope. Remove the redundant lookup on Save without weakening validation. Preserve the distinction between a successful snapshot declaring no requirement and a failed capability lookup, reusing current recovery/error presentation. No new endpoint, bridge callback, component, provider-specific validation framework or duplicate operation implementation.

Acceptance criteria
- BO data-source draft validation does not directly invoke Bridge.capability_snapshot or concrete adapter capability inspection.
- Cached facts used for feedback originate from the existing routed capability lookup, with provider/selected-connection scope preserved where applicable.
- The PR-added Save path no longer repeats the same capability inspection unnecessarily. Authoritative validation remains effective and routed when fresh facts are needed.
- A declared webhook/watch requirement still rejects missing global base URL; a successful snapshot without that requirement remains accepted.
- Lookup failure is explicitly unavailable/recoverable and is not silently interpreted as no requirement. Preserve drafts and avoid indiscriminately blocking unrelated operations.
- Extend the existing base-URL validation tests with focused call-count/boundary assertions showing no local bridge lookup during draft validation. Add only distinct failure/routing cases needed; reuse existing fixtures and assertions.
- Preserve existing test intent; obtain explicit approval before changing existing behavioral expectations under docs/testing-approach.md. Do not change tests merely to hide regressions.
- Run mix q and isolated relevant suites through Context Mode. Follow parent validation/UX/E2E gates. This issue does not authorize commits, pushes, merges or restarting final precommit previously deferred by the user.

Agent handoff
Read AGENTS.md, docs/agent-tools.md, docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md, docs/action-reuse.md, docs/testing-approach.md, docs/code-quality.md, docs/conventions.md, docs/architecture.md and applicable Channels/Engine service sections. If changing UI presentation, read DESIGN.md and docs/bo-components.md first. Read module responsibilities before editing. Limit work to finding 3; findings 1 and 2 are zaq-h2i.3.15 and zaq-h2i.3.16. Coordinate shared capability-loading edits with .16 without introducing speculative dependencies. User requested issue creation only in this turn; no implementation or agent delegation was performed.


Scope clarification agreed during review discussion
Reduce redundant capability lookups and duplicate capability assigns as part of this issue. "Draft" means existing unsaved form values/changesets; do not introduce a capability-draft mechanism, another validation layer, or new data-source proposal handling for this finding.

File capabilities are already the file_delivery subtree of the normal capability snapshot. SMTP's file_capabilities_snapshot currently holds a whole snapshot, while capabilities_snapshot serves the dialog. Their current distinction is provider versus selected-connector scope, not a separate file capability contract.

Preferred simplification
- Use one authoritative presentation snapshot for the current editor selection: exact selected-connector scope for an existing connector; provider scope for a new connector until proposal-specific validation is necessary.
- Reuse that snapshot for the capability dialog, file controls and base-URL feedback. Derive file metadata and other cheap presentation values rather than storing parallel copies.
- Before merging assigns, verify whether the dialog intentionally promises provider-wide facts. Preserve that contract or explicitly document any necessary scope distinction; do not silently substitute a different connector/provider scope just to reduce assign count.
- Load on opening/selecting an editor when the appropriate snapshot is not already available. Reuse the cached result for typing, tab switches and opening a dialog with a valid snapshot. Refresh when selection changes, on explicit retry, or through the rejected-save recovery tracked in zaq-h2i.3.16. Do not reuse a snapshot for the wrong selection or scope.
- Keep lookup status explicit: successful empty/unsupported capabilities must remain distinguishable from unavailable capabilities. Use the simplest existing state shape; do not add a generalized caching framework or needless state wrappers.
- Retain current-fact validation of the effective proposal at the owning save boundary. Eliminating duplicate presentation requests does not authorize trusting stale page facts for persistence. This issue does not require an additional save-validation layer.

Additional verification
Extend existing tests with assertions that typing, tab switching and opening the capability dialog reuse the loaded snapshot; changing connector selection obtains the correct scoped facts; retry and .16 recovery refresh without losing drafts. Verify both dialog and file controls use the selected snapshot and preserve successful-empty versus failed-lookup behavior. Prefer adding assertions to existing scenarios over duplicating setup or adding separate tests for each rendering consumer.

comments.text: Source audit found an explicit existing SMTP test requiring provider scope even for a selected connector. Proposed single snapshot uses exact selected scope (and provider scope for new/unselected); requested specific human approval before updating that assertion, retry counts, and cached webhook-validation setup. No existing test behavior has been changed. Current isolated editor run: 132/135 pass; three failures correspond exactly to those pending contract changes. Source implementation in progress; not claiming validation complete.

Human approval received in this conversation: update SMTP retry lookup counts 2→3→5→5 to 2→3→4→4; load webhook-test facts through routed editor opening then verify zero typing lookups; use exact selected SMTP scope in dialog and file controls while retaining provider scope for new/unselected SMTP and existing IMAP provider scope. All display/validation/draft assertions retained.

Boundary/cache implementation verified: routed selected/provider facts; no direct BO bridge inspection; draft/tab/dialog use cache; data-source saves requiring missing-base-URL decisions inspect current facts once; failed lookup stays recoverable. SMTP now has one snapshot and one lookup per selection/retry; dialog scope approved and documented. Existing widget closed-editor provider retry contract retained. Editor suites passed in latest combined run (308/309 total; sole failure was new component whitespace assertion, now corrected). Self-review found nil response handling in new shared helper; fixed to preserve unavailable versus absent validation metadata and added regression.
